intro: Uzbekistan is home to the great Silk Road cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva, once among the richest and most learned places on Earth.

chapters.title: Silk Road cities
text: Sogdian merchants from Samarkand and Bukhara dominated Silk Road trade between China and Persia. Alexander the Great conquered the region in the 320s BC and married Roxana, a local princess.
Arab armies brought Islam in the 700s. Bukhara became a great centre of learning, home to scholars like Avicenna and al-Bukhari, and al-Khwarizmi, who gave us the word 'algorithm', came from Khorezm.

chapters.title: Timur and his heirs
text: Genghis Khan destroyed many cities in 1220. In the 1300s Timur (Tamerlane) built a vast empire with Samarkand as its glittering capital, decorated with blue-tiled domes. His grandson Ulugh Beg built a great observatory there.
Later Uzbek khanates ruled from Bukhara, Khiva and Kokand.

highlight.title: Registan
highlight.text: Samarkand's Registan square, framed by three tiled madrasas, is one of the wonders of Islamic architecture.

chapters.title: Russian rule and independence
text: Russia conquered the khanates in the 1860s and 1870s. In Soviet times, huge cotton farms drained the rivers feeding the Aral Sea, causing an environmental disaster.
Uzbekistan became independent in 1991. Islam Karimov ruled harshly until his death in 2016; his successor Shavkat Mirziyoyev has opened up the economy.
